entries.name: Blue Zone route planning
entries.summary: The white circle indicates the destination for the shrinking play area.
body: Check your position, the white circle and the phase timer together. Remaining in the damaging zone costs health; exact timing and damage depend on the current mode.
Choose a route with reachable cover before continuing to loot. Recheck the map after each circle change instead of following an old marker blindly.

entries.name: Attachment compatibility
entries.summary: An attachment only transfers when the replacement weapon supports it.
body: Gameplay settings control automatic attachment behavior for pickups and weapon replacement. Incompatible parts remain in the inventory rather than equipping to the new gun.
After changing weapons, inspect the actual slots and ammunition before leaving cover. A familiar sight in your bag is not proof that it is mounted.

entries.name: Emergency Pickup deployment
entries.summary: An aerial relocation item needs open space and a planned landing.
body: Deploy where the balloon has clear sky and no nearby obstacles, then attach before the aircraft arrives. During transport you can detach and parachute to a selected landing.
Passengers remain vulnerable. Check current mode availability and circle restrictions in-game; the linked introduction documents the mechanism, not today’s spawn pool.

entries.name: Aim/Sound Lab
entries.summary: Private training separates aiming practice from directional sound practice.
body: Use a Lab access point in Training Mode and select aiming or sound practice. Sound exercises ask you to identify where a played gunshot came from.
Keep volume and headphones consistent between attempts. Change one setting at a time and compare results so a better score has a useful explanation.

entries.name: Carry a knocked teammate
entries.summary: Carrying repositions a downed player; reviving is a separate action.
body: Approach without sprinting and use your Limited Interact binding to pick up or put down the teammate. Choose a clear landing space before carrying.
Check nearby threats and the zone first. After reaching cover, put the player down and perform the normal revive interaction if conditions allow.

entries.name: Reviving at the water surface
entries.summary: A knocked swimmer can be revived at the surface, not underwater.
body: Both players must remain above water during the revive. Submerging or moving too much cancels it; a downed player is still losing health.
Agree on a nearby surface position or shore before approaching. Water does not provide reliable protection from opponents, so reassess whether the rescue is possible.

entries.name: Deston fuel pumps
entries.summary: A usable pump refuels a stopped vehicle while the driver stays seated.
body: Stop near an undamaged pump and use the driver’s interaction prompt. Moving the vehicle or changing seats interrupts refueling.
Damaged pumps can explode and destroyed pumps cannot refuel. Choose the stopping position before approaching and leave once your fuel plan is satisfied.

entries.name: Screen and map pings
entries.summary: A visible marker helps a squad agree on one location.
body: Aim at the intended location and use your ping binding, or place a map marker. Verify the marker landed on the intended surface rather than something closer.
Update the marker when the situation changes. A location ping is a callout, not ongoing enemy tracking; pair it with a short description when useful.
